task_name: The live sessions the backend lists

rubric.result: The objective promises `GET /sessions` answers the sessions the backend owns, each one named. Taken apart: (a) a route at `/sessions` answering GET — `sessions-route.ts` declares `PATH = '/sessions'`, `METHOD = 'GET'` and a handler, and `api-server.ts` mounts `app.get(SessionsRoute.PATH, Browsers.turnAwayForeign, SessionsRoute.handledBy(this.listLiveSessions!))` just before `app.use(Failures.nothingMatched)`; (b) the sessions the backend owns — `ListLiveSessions.execute()` asks the `LiveSessions` port's `all()` and wraps it in `ListLiveSessionsResult`; (c) each one named — `LiveSession` carries `id` and `name`, both guarded non-blank, and the route projects `{id, name}` per session at 200. Every part of the sentence has production lines behind it, exercised over a real listening server. The API.md section and the `API_PATHS` entry the endpoint will also need belong to tasks 9 and 6 of this plan, not to this one.

The TDD line names `it('the live sessions the backend owns are listed with their names')` and fixes the limit as: a port holding two sessions answers both, in its own order, each as `{id, name}` and nothing else. The test in `sessions-route.test.ts:228` arranges two sessions (`session-1`/`zsh`, `session-2`/`claude`), asks the running server, and asserts `response.status === 200` plus `toEqual({sessions: [{id:'session-1',name:'zsh'},{id:'session-2',name:'claude'}]})` — `toEqual` on the parsed body pins both entries, their order, and that each carries those two keys and nothing else. Same assertion, same input, same expected value. One nuance weighed and dismissed: the sessions are held by a double of the use case rather than of the port, which is what `conventions/testing.md` prescribes for a controller ("Controller | the use case, by construction") and what the exemplar `external-tools-route.test.ts` does; the number of sessions, their order and the projected shape — which is what the plan's sentence fixes — are unchanged.

Four Contract blocks plus a Current state block, compared symbol by symbol. `LiveSession`: `readonly id: string`, `readonly name: string`, `constructor({ id, name }: { id: unknown, name: unknown })` — identical, and it freezes itself (`Object.freeze(this)`) as the prose demands. `LiveSessions`: `export type LiveSessionStream = { readonly printed: string, readonly stop: () => void }` verbatim, and `all()`, `find(id: string)`, `watch({ session, onBytes })`, `write({ session, text })` with the declared parameter names, order and return types, all synchronous, each refusing with `${this.constructor.name} must implement …()` exactly as `tool-sessions.ts` does. `ListLiveSessionsResult` carries `readonly sessions: readonly LiveSession[]`; `ListLiveSessions` takes `{ liveSessions }` by name and `execute(): ListLiveSessionsResult`. `SessionsRoute` declares `static readonly PATH = '/sessions'`, `static readonly METHOD = 'GET'`, `static handledBy(listLiveSessions: ListLiveSessions): RequestHandler` and `static refuseOtherMethods(request, response): void`. `api-server.ts` gains the `listLiveSessions` collaborator and the `app.get` + `app.all` pair in the shape of the cited `ExternalToolsRoute` lines, immediately before `app.use(Failures.nothingMatched)`. The answer is 200 `{"sessions":[{"id":"…","name":"…"}]}` in the port's order. Nothing states something else.

Rows the diff bears on: P-1 (the port is synchronous — `all`, `find`, `watch` and `write` return without a promise, so the stream route can write headers between finding and the first byte) is implemented exactly: no `async`, no `Promise` in any of the four signatures, and `ListLiveSessions.execute()` is synchronous too. D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) — all five new modules and both new tests are `.ts`. P-8 (identifiers, test names and log lines in English) — every identifier, test name and error message in the diff is English; no product copy is added. P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session) — the diff adds only a GET and its 405 refusal; no `POST /sessions`, no delete. P-6 and P-7 belong to the adapter of task 2 and P-2, P-9 to tasks 4 and 5; the diff implements nothing that bears on them. No row is reopened with a different value.

Exemplars: the diff is a faithful imitation of the ones §3 names. `sessions-route.ts` follows `external-tools-route.ts` line for line — the two static constants, `handledBy` returning the handler, the inline projection to the wire shape, and `refuseOtherMethods` setting `Allow` before `Answer.refuse(response, 405, 'method-not-allowed', 'method not allowed')`. `live-sessions.ts` follows `tool-sessions.ts` (a port refusing until an adapter implements it); `live-session.ts` follows `tool-session.ts` (validates in the constructor quoting what it got, then `Object.freeze(this)`); `list-live-sessions.ts` follows `survey-external-tools.ts` (result object frozen over a copied array, port by name through the constructor); `sessions-route.test.ts` reproduces `external-tools-route.test.ts`'s `RunningApi` harness, `Answered` type and `afterEach` teardown. RULES — architecture.md: the three layers show in the tree (`domain/value-objects`, `domain/ports`, `application/queries`, `infrastructure/`), the direction holds (domain imports nobody; the query imports only domain types; the route imports application), one controller per endpoint plus one line that wires it in, the use case takes its dependency through the constructor by name and declares its result object even carrying a single field, no suffix on type or result. domain.md: `LiveSessions`/`LiveSession` name what the domain needs, not the tool — swapping node-pty for anything else leaves the names true — and the value object guards its own invariant (non-blank id and name) and stays guarded 'even on the day every caller already satisfies it'. boundaries.md: the code of the 405 is declared explicitly beside its detail and never derived from a class name; there is no cast, no inbound payload to validate, and the outer edge (`api-server.ts`) is where the collaborator is injected. decisions.md: no business rule is written twice — the 405/`method-not-allowed` shape is the boundary idiom every one of the nine routes already carries, 'the same sentence, not the same decision'. this-repository.md: relative imports name the real `.ts` extension, erasable syntax only, `{code, detail}` kebab-case with 405 kept for the protocol. DEFECTS.MD, RULE BY RULE — (1) closed vocabulary: no subject. `id` and `name` are an identifier and a label, not values that classify; the diff adds no boolean derived from a vocabulary and no dispatch, so no catch-all branch exists to find. (2) raw map as the return value of logic: complies. The query returns `ListLiveSessionsResult`, never a map; the only object literal is built inside `Answer.send(response, 200, {…})` in the route, which is the last step before the wire and is one step — nothing downstream decides anything with it. (3) two fields that have to agree / sentinel: complies. `LiveSession`'s two fields are independent, there is no flag repeating another field, and absence is never spelled with a sentinel — no live session is the empty array `{"sessions":[]}` at 200, asserted as such, rather than an empty string, a zero or a refusal. (4) an error named for where it happens: no subject. The diff declares no error type; it throws `Error` with messages naming what happened (`a live session's id must be a non-empty string, got …`, `LiveSessions must implement all()`), never the module. DELIVERY AND BOUNDARIES: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for a new endpoint here, and the change is additive — no existing signature, constructor or public contract is altered for a caller already on the old path (`listLiveSessions` enters `ApiCollaborators` optional, like the fourteen collaborators beside it, so every existing construction of `ApiServer` still compiles). ONE CLASH, DECLARED AND LEFT OUT OF THE FINDINGS: `conventions/simplicity.md` asks 'which call breaks without it? Name it. If none does, it goes', and says in as many words that 'a plan can ask for a field that no caller in the tree uses — that gap is measured here'. `find`, `watch`, `write` and the exported `LiveSessionStream` have no caller in this diff; their callers arrive in tasks 4 and 5 of this same slice. The implementer could not have written it otherwise: the plan handed that four-method port as a verbatim Contract block for THIS task, so dropping three methods would have been a `contrato` finding instead. Two rubric items cannot both be satisfied, so it is reported here and not as a finding — and the implementer did exactly what that document prescribes for the case ('Where the burden cannot be discharged, that is declared in the task's report … and the decision is left to a person'). The cost is bounded: an unimplemented method throws a message naming itself rather than answering undefined. The same treatment for one smaller mismatch: the three test names are prose-with-spaces while this repo's committed tests use snake_case, but the names are literals the plan's `**TDD:**`/`**Tests:**` pinned and `ct-step controls` grepped for, and `conventions/testing.md` asks only that the name be the sentence, which they are.

Does not apply: no pre-existing test was touched. Both test files in the diff are new (`new file mode 100644`), and the only modified file is `backend/src/infrastructure/api-server.ts`, production code. Its two `-` lines are the reflow of the constructor's destructuring list forced by the new `listLiveSessions` parameter — no assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten anywhere in the diff.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. Revert `sessions-route.ts` and the three route tests fail at the request (404, no `Allow` header); revert the six added lines of `api-server.ts` and the same happens; revert `list-live-sessions.ts` and both suites fail to import. The route test's double (`ListLiveSessionsSpy`) replaces only the use case, which is the seam `conventions/testing.md` prescribes for a controller, and the assertion is on the wire — status, headers and the literal JSON body of a real server reached with a real `fetch` — not on the double. The query test's `LiveSessionsDouble` replaces only the port, and the assertion is on what the real `ListLiveSessions` returned (`toBeInstanceOf(ListLiveSessionsResult)` and the sessions in the port's order). No expected value is hard-coded in a place that would survive the production lines being removed.

Every line serves a sentence of the task. The five new modules and the two new test files are each named in `**Files:**` and each contains only the symbols the Contract blocks describe. Inside `api-server.ts` the change is exactly the collaborator the task asks for: two imports, one optional field on `ApiCollaborators`, one readonly field, one name in the constructor's destructuring and one assignment, and the `app.get` + `app.all` pair — plus the reflow of two destructuring lines, which is forced by adding a name to that same list and keeps the file's line width. Nothing out of `### Out of scope` is touched: the eight existing endpoints keep their paths, bodies, codes and answers untouched (no existing route file, request model or refusal is modified), no session is opened or killed, no second frame kind is declared and no command travels from the browser. No refactor, rename, adjacent fix or extra helper rides along; `backend/API.md` and `frontend/vite.config.ts` — which this endpoint will eventually need — are correctly left for tasks 9 and 6 that declare them. No hunk of the plan file appears in the diff, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Six new tests, all three properties held. DETERMINISTIC: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep; the only I/O is a `fetch` to `127.0.0.1` on the port the server was given by asking for `port: 0`, and `frontendRoot` points at a path under `tmpdir()` that is only ever tested for existence. The same code makes them pass tomorrow. ISOLATED: each test builds its own `ApiServer` and its own spy; the one piece of shared mutable state, `RunningApi.#started`, is drained by `afterEach(async () => { await RunningApi.stopAll() })`, which splices the array and stops every server, so no port, file or directory is taken for granted and no test needs an order from the rest of the file. VERIFIES REAL BEHAVIOUR: every assertion is on what production code did — the status, the `allow` header and the literal JSON body a real listening server wrote, and the result object the real `ListLiveSessions` built; none would still pass with this diff's production lines reverted. `expect(spy.asked).toBe(0)` is the one assertion on a double, and `conventions/testing.md` requires it by name ('A refusal never reaches a double: every controller test of a refused request also asserts that the use case was not asked'); it sits beside three assertions on the real answer. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` to measure the finer half against the text the implementer was given and found nothing to report under it: the tests use real code with the single double the layer's rule prescribes, each name describes a behaviour rather than a method, and the one name carrying an 'and' ('no live session is an empty list and not a refusal') is a single behaviour stated with its contrast — and is in any case a literal the plan pinned. The mother idiom is honoured (`LiveSessionMother.zsh()`/`.claude()`, named scenarios; `ListLiveSessionsSpy.answeringTwoSessions()`/`.answeringNoSessions()`), and the literals repeated in the route test are the payload the boundary assertion has to state literally, exactly as the named exemplar `external-tools-route.test.ts` does.
